title: NBC Comedy ‘Newlyweds’ Casts Emma Meisel, Ignacio Diaz-Silverio, Bill O’Neill
description:
NBC‘s new multi-cam comedy “Newlyweds” has cast three new series regulars, Variety has learned. 

	Emma Meisel, Ignacio Diaz-Silverio and Bill O’Nei
body:
NBC‘s new multi-cam comedy “Newlyweds” has cast three new series regulars, Variety has learned. 

	Emma Meisel, Ignacio Diaz-Silverio and Bill O’Neill have all joined the series opposite leads Téa Leoni and Tim Daly. As previously reported, series executive producer Jamie Lee Curtis will also appear in a recurring guest star role. 

	The logline for the show describes it as “a later-in-life love story about a free-spirited woman (Leoni) and a buttoned-up professor (Daly) who marry impetuously after a whirlwind courtship.” 
	

	Meisel and Diaz-Silverio will play Poppy and Lolo, respectively. Both are Jeanie’s (Leoni), with Lolo being adopted. O’Neill will play Arvid, who is James’ (Daly) assistant in the philosophy department at the University of Oslo.


	Meisel previously appeared in the Disney+ series “Doogie Kamealoha, M.D.” She is also known for her role in Destry Allyn Spielberg’s debut film, “Please Don’t Feed the Children” and appeared in multiple episodes of “American Horror Story” Season 9. 

	She is repped by Innovative Artists and MGMT Entertainment. 

	Diaz-Silverio is best known for starring in the critically-acclaimed Amazon series “Primo” from Shea Serrano and Mike Schur. He has since appeared in shows like “Zero Day,” “Law & Order: SVU,” and “FBI.” His film credits include Zach Braff’s ““A Good Person.”

	He is repped by Gersh and Untitled Entertainment. 

	O’Neill’s “The Amazing Banana Brothers” earned him an Edinburgh Comedy Award nomination for Best Newcomer at the Edinburgh Fringe. He is also a co-creator of the FX show “Two Pink Doors” and is featured in Edgar Wright’s remake of “The Running Man.” 
	

	He is repped by UTA and Venture Entertainment Partners. 

	“Newlyweds” hails from writer and executive producer Gail Lerner as well as executive producers Eric and Kim Tannenbaum for The Tannenbaum Company, Curtis, Scott Schwartz, and Lionsgate Television. Pam Fryman directed and executive produced the pilot. Universal Television is the studio. 

	“Newlyweds” is one of just two new comedies that NBC picked up for the 2026-2027 broadcast season, with the other being the single-cam laffer “Sunset P.I.” “Newlyweds” will premiere this fall, while “Sunset P.I.” will be held for midseason.

schema.headline: NBC Comedy ‘Newlyweds’ Casts Emma Meisel, Ignacio Diaz-Silverio, Bill O’Neill

title: Ryan Gosling Pitched His Own ‘Ghost Rider’ Movie to Marvel as Studio Slows Down Output to Restore Quality: ‘When Quantity Is So Much, You Get Spread Thin’
description: Marvel’s buzzy Comic-Con presentation put two huge comic book movie tentpoles on the studio’s 2028 release calendar: “Black Panther 3,” featuring th
body:
Marvel’s buzzy Comic-Con presentation put two huge comic book movie tentpoles on the studio’s 2028 release calendar: “Black Panther 3,” featuring the debut of David Jonnson as T’Challa II/Toussaint, and “Ghost Rider,” starring Ryan Gosling in the title role. The announcement means “Spider-Man: Brand New day,” “Avengers: Doomsday” and “Avengers: Secret Wars” will be the only Marvel movies released in theaters between now and 2028. In fact, “Secret Wars” is the only 2027 Marvel movie release.
	

	“A lot of it is a strategy we’ve talked about for a while, of focusing on quality,” Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige told Empire magazine at Comic-Con about the sparser release calendar. “We always try to focus on quality, but when quantity is so much, you get spread thin. We didn’t want to be spread thin, and the Avengers is as important as it comes. And ‘Secret Wars’… is a setup in and of itself to the future, to what’s next. So really, it was landing those two movies and setting up 2028, of which we’ve revealed two of them so far, ‘Ghost Rider’ and ‘Panther III.'”


	With the television series “VisionQuest” arriving on Disney+ in October, the Marvel Cinematic Universe will be getting a total of four new entries across two years. That’s a massive slow down from the exhaustive output Marvel previously delivered across theaters and streaming. There were six Marvel movie and TV projects in 2023 alone, for instance. Feige previously admitted to Variety that Marvel’s “over-expansion” into Disney+ streaming content was the start of “quantity trumping quality” at the studio, which he now seems to be actively course-correcting.
	

	Disney’s former CEO Bob Iger also cited Marvel’s push into streaming as a reason for its disappointing critical and commercial run across 2023 and 2024, explaining: “They had not been in the TV business at any significant level. Not only did they increase their movie output, but they ended up making a number of television series, and frankly, it diluted focus and attention. That is, I think, more of the cause than anything.”

	Marvel is now slowing down its output in an attempt to restore its quality. While the studio is currently developing a new take on the X-Men, the standalone movie’s release date was not announced at Comic-Con. Feige told Empire that Gosling’s “Ghost Rider” movie moved ahead after “it was Gosling who had the vision. It was Gosling who had the pitch that won over Shawn, that had them come and pitch us this idea, which led to us on stage today.”

	Shawn Levy is directing the “Ghost Rider” movie after working together with Gosling on the upcoming “Star Wars: Starfigher.” Disney owns both the Marvel and Star Wars franchises.

schema.headline: Ryan Gosling Pitched His Own ‘Ghost Rider’ Movie to Marvel as Studio Slows Down Output to Restore Quality: ‘When Quantity Is So Much, You Get Spread Thin’

title: Canal+ Seals Landmark Pact to Invest Nearly $1.1 Billion in French and European Films
description: Canal+ has reached a five-year deal with French cinema organizations which will see the pay-TV powerhouse invest nearly €1 billion ($1.1 billion) in
body:
Canal+ has reached a five-year deal with French cinema organizations which will see the pay-TV powerhouse invest nearly €1 billion ($1.1 billion) in French and European films between 2028 and 2032.

	Canal+ Chairman and CEO Maxime Saada announced the deal in a post on X, describing the agreement as “historic,” reaffirming Canal+’s position as the leading partner of the French and European film industries.


	“French cinema, the most dynamic in Europe and among the world’s leading film industries, deserves to be supported, financed and championed,” Saada wrote, adding that Canal+, which has backed the sector for more than 40 years, would continue to do so “with pride.”
	

Très heureux d’annoncer un nouvel accord historique entre @CANAL+ et les organisations du cinéma français.Près d’1 milliard d’euros investis par CANAL+ sur une durée inédite de 5 ans, entre 2028 et 2032, dans le cinéma français et européen. Un engagement historique à la hauteur…— Maxime Saada (@maxsaada) July 27, 2026


	It’s an improvement from the latest three-year agreement which saw Canal+ committing to investing €480 million from 2025 to 2027. The amount also integrates obligations tied to OCS, a formerly rival pay TV group which Canal+ bought in 2023. OSC previously had a pact with French orgs to invest least €60 million on French and European film between 2021 and 2023. 

	Saada also said Canal+ would continue to offer subscribers films six months after their theatrical release, indicating that the agreement preserves the banner’s place in France’s media chronology.

	The agreement follows months of negotiations over Canal+‘s future investment obligations under France’s media chronology, which links broadcasters’ financial commitments to the timing of their access to theatrical releases. The talks unfolded as Netflix and Prime Video have appealed the country’s Council of State to challenge the longstanding financing and release-window system which forces them to wait 17 months to access newly released films. Streamers are arguing that their investment levels should entitle them to earlier access to films. Saada, meanwhile, has been lobbying to obtain an even more favorable window for Canal+ Group, pointing that Disney+ seized a 9-month window with a €35 million investment in theatrical movies.
	

	Negotiations for this pact unfolded during tense times between Canal+ Group and the French film industry, especially at the Cannes Film Festival, during which a petition criticizing the growing influence  of Vincent Bolloré, the banner’s biggest shareholder, over French media and accusing him of having a fascist agenda. Saada hit back during a luncheon with French producers at Cannes, telling the crowd Canal+ would no longer be working with signatories. His remarks prompted accusations of blacklisting from industry groups and leading thousands more film professionals to add their names to the open letter, notably Javier Bardem and Mark Ruffalo. 

	Saada then clarified his statements during an annual general in late May and said Canal+ “wouldn’t be hunting down” technicians or refusing to finance films because individuals had signed the petition. He nevertheless revealed filmmakers’ relationship with Canal+ would become a factor in the company’s assessment of projects, saying the broadcaster would consider whether people behind a film had “actively caused harm” to the company.

	Canal+ Group was at Cannes with six movies – notably Quentin Dupieux’s “Full Phil” starring Kristen Stewart and Woody Harrelson, and Jeanne Herry’s “Garance” starring Adèle Exarchopoulos — and will next be attending the Venice Film Festival with several films, including the opening night movie, Danny Boyle‘s “Ink” starring Guy Pearce and Jack O’Connell.

schema.headline: Canal+ Seals Landmark Pact to Invest Nearly $1.1 Billion in French and European Films

title: BuzzFeed Laying Off 35% of Its Employees After Byron Allen Takes Over Company
description: BuzzFeed is slashing its workforce on the heels of the digital media company’s deal to sell a controlling ownership stake to entrepreneur and comedi
body:
BuzzFeed is slashing its workforce on the heels of the digital media company’s deal to sell a controlling ownership stake to entrepreneur and comedian Byron Allen.

	The company disclosed that it is laying off about 35% of its current employees and contractors. “The reduction in workforce plan is intended to advance the Company’s path towards profitability and positive cash flow generation by streamlining its organizational structure, optimizing operating expenses, and preserving cash,” BuzzFeed said in an SEC filing Monday.
	

	The move will eliminate about 180 jobs across BuzzFeed, including at its HuffPost and Tasty divisions. As of Dec. 31, 2025, BuzzFeed had 507 employees located across five countries, per its annual report filed with the SEC.


	BuzzFeed estimates it will incur between $6.5 million to $8.5 million in charges related to the job cuts, expected to recognized primarily in the third quarter of 2026. With the layoffs, the company said, it expects to realize annualized savings of $29 million-$32 million.

	Under the terms of BuzzFeed’s agreement with Allen, his company acquired a 51% stake in the company for a total purchase price of $120 million. The deal closed in late May. The transaction was funded with $20 million in cash at closing and a $100 million promissory note due five years from closing, accruing interest at 5% annually.

	Allen has said he plans to use BuzzFeed and HuffPost to build a free-streaming platform with premium and user-generated content that he imagines will rival YouTube. Asked how he will turn things around at BuzzFeed, Allen told Variety earlier this year, “I’ve done much harder things. They don’t have problems that are that big. The money is the easy part. The strategy is to really grow this.”
	

	Allen is also chairman and CEO of Allen Media Group, which owns 13 ABC, CBS and NBC network affiliate broadcast television stations and 10 HD television networks serving nearly 275 million subscribers, including the Weather Channel. The exec said he would combine BuzzFeed and HuffPost with Allen Media’s Local Now, a streaming service that delivers localized content. “We can immediately help them bring in ad dollars,” Allen said. “Free streaming is the fastest-growing thing. The ad dollars are moving rapidly from cable to streaming… The two best words in the world are ‘free’ and ‘streaming.’”

	In addition, Allen has leased a two-hour nightly comedy block on CBS and has taken over the time-slot previously occupied by “Late Night With Stephen Colbert” with episodes of “Comics Unleashed With Byron Allen,” followed by comedy show “Funny You Should Ask.”

schema.headline: BuzzFeed Laying Off 35% of Its Employees After Byron Allen Takes Over Company

title: Gold House Launches Gold House Studios, Unveiling A Slate Led By ‘The Boys’ Star Karen Fukuhara (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Gold House, the cultural platform behind the Gold Open movement and The Gold Gala is moving into production with the launch of Gold House Studios.
body:
Gold House, the cultural platform behind the Gold Open movement and The Gold Gala is moving into production with the launch of Gold House Studios.

	Since its launch eight years ago, Gold House has been one of the most influential forces in entertainment and culture. The company has campaigned over 800 openings for films like “Crazy Rich Asians” and “Everything Everywhere All At Once.” With Gold House Studios, its focus will be on developing and producing original and IP-driven stories across film, television, and digital media.
	

	Gold House Studios will be led by Gold House veterans Christine Yi and Brian Nemes, with Yi heading the studio and Nemes leading IP and Development. Both will serve as producers for all projects on the Gold House Studio’s slate.


	“Too many great films pull off a small miracle to get made only to go unseen,” says Yi, who previously led operations at Gold House Ventures, Gold House’s tech VC fund, and still acts as General Manager of Gold House Labs, the foundation’s talent development programs. “As an impact-driven company, one of our top priorities is to develop compelling stories with leading roles for Asian Pacific talent and rich, nuanced, cultural context that feels novel or unexpected. But our highest priority measure of ‘impact’ will be our ability to reach audiences and resonate well beyond our own community.”

	The slate leads with “Akiya” starring Karen Fukuhara (“The Boys”) and Robbie Amell (“Upload,” “Code 8”), which follows a married couple who move to Japan to renovate an “akiya”, an unoccupied countryside home, only to discover the house is haunted by Japanese folklore creatures called yōkai and a demon woman named Yotsume Baba. The film will be written and directed by Austin Osanai Everett and produced alongside Ranger 7 and Collective Pictures.
	

	“This Way to Home” is also on the slate, and is a road trip dramedy from writer-director Mel Mah.

	On the TV side, the studio is developing “American Yokai,” an atmospheric horror from Keto Shimizu, the showrunner who steered “Legends of Tomorrow.”

	IP-led projects will also be in focus at Gold House Studios. In another partnership with Ranger 7, JEA, and Striker Entertainment, Gold House has secured film rights to “Slitterhead,” the cult Japanese game from Bokeh Game Studio created by Keiichiro Toyama, creator of Silent Hill. Gold House has indicated many more IP-inspired projects are in the pipeline, though details remain under wraps.

	On the unscripted side, Gold House has a digital series set to begin filming in New York City later this year.

	 Prior work in financing and production include Sean Wang’s “Didi,” Vera Miao’s “Rock Springs,” and Grammy winner Laufey’s music video for “Madwoman.”

	“For years, Gold House has helped prove that culture isn’t a niche nor decorative—it’s mainstream infrastructure. Gold House Studios reflects our belief that stories remain the most powerful force for human connection. In a time when audiences are fragmented across platforms, algorithms, and identities, great storytelling still has the ability to bring strangers into the same conversation, the same emotion, and the same future.” said Bing Chen, Gold House CEO & Co-Founder.

schema.headline: Gold House Launches Gold House Studios, Unveiling A Slate Led By ‘The Boys’ Star Karen Fukuhara (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘The Odyssey’ by the Numbers: 6 Ways Christopher Nolan’s Epic Is Shattering Box Office Expectations
description:
With a sensational second weekend at the box office, it’s clear “The Odyssey” will have a long — and epic — journey in theaters.

	Christopher Nolan
body:
With a sensational second weekend at the box office, it’s clear “The Odyssey” will have a long — and epic — journey in theaters.

	Christopher Nolan‘s take on Homer’s 3,000-year-old poem, starring Matt Damon as the Greek king Odysseus, has generated a remarkable $652 million worldwide, including $289 million domestically and $362 million internationally after just 10 days of release. It’s already the sixth-highest grossing Hollywood movie of the year at the global box office — no small feat for a sword-and-sandal epic that’s rated R and clocks in at nearly three hours.
	

	With euphoric word-of-mouth and staggering demand for premium large formats like Imax, “The Odyssey” is expected to shatter all kinds of records throughout the rest of summer and into the fall. It could overtake 2009’s “The Dark Knight” ($1.008 billion) and 2012’s “The Dark Knight Rises” ($1.08 billion) as Nolan’s highest-grossing film. Depending on staying power and the turnout in China (it doesn’t open there until Aug. 14), “The Odyssey” could eventually surpass 2024’s “Deadpool & Wolverine” ($1.33 billion) as the largest R-rated release in history. And it’s on pace to rank among Imax’s biggest triumphs, though the all-time benchmark set by 2009’s “Avatar” ($270 million) might be tough to beat.


	“’The Odyssey’ has crossed over from hit blockbuster to global cultural event,” Imax’s CEO Richard Gelfond said over the weekend.

	As “The Odyssey” continues its grand big-screen voyage, here are six ways to contextualize the big-budget movie’s massive commercial success.
	
	
		1. “The Odyssey” earned more in its second weekend than most of this year’s movies did in their first	

	“The Odyssey” scored a stellar $90 million in its sophomore outing, a barely-there 27% decline from its $123.5 million debut. (Most tentpoles that open above $100 million would decline by 50% or more in subsequent weekends.) Just how significant is that second-weekend haul? Hits like “The Devil Wears Prada 2” ($76 million) and “Project Hail Mary” ($80 million) didn’t even generate that much to start. In fact, only three other movies in 2026 — “Toy Story 5,” “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” and “Michael — earned above $90 million in their opening weekends. In terms of records, “The Odyssey” marks the biggest second weekend of the year, ahead of “Toy Story 5” with $70 million, as well as the second-largest second weekend ever for an R-rated movie, following “Deadpool & Wolverine” with $96 million in its sophomore outing. And those two films hail from major franchises, not a centuries-old poem.
	
		2. Second weekend ticket sales were bigger than the start of “Oppenheimer” 	

	Three summers ago, “Oppenheimer” launched above expectations to $82 million, a significant chunk of change for a historical drama that’s heavy on talking and light on action. It’s no surprise “The Odyssey” loomed much larger in its debut, but it’s a testament to Nolan’s box office durability that second-weekend sales were bigger than the opening of “Oppenheimer.” His biopic about the father of the atomic bomb left theaters with a sizable $330 million in North America and $975 million globally, so there’s no telling where ticket sales for “The Odyssey” will top out.
	
		3. Imax ticket sales hit $140 million after two weekends of release	

	“The Odyssey” has been a juggernaut in Imax with $140 million globally, becoming the company’s second-fastest film to reach $100 million after clearing the benchmark in 10 days. Only 2019’s behemoth “Avengers: Endgame” was quicker to the milestone. And “The Odyssey” hasn’t even landed in major international markets including China, Japan and Korea. To put those revenues in context, “Oppenheimer” was considered a massive success with $180 million in Imax by the end of its theatrical run. Given the goodwill from “Oppenheimer,” Nolan’s penchant for the format, and the reality that many Imax showtimes are sold out into September, “The Odyssey” will surpass the lifetime Imax haul of “Oppenheimer” after less than a month in theaters.
	
	
		4. “The Odyssey” has generated around the same as all of Sony, Warner Bros. and Paramount’s 2026 films combined	

	That’s right — one of Universal’s movies (a non-franchise film, for that matter) has amassed more than the entire slates from three major studios — Warner Bros. ($622.6 million across seven movies including “The Bride!” and “Supergirl”), Sony ($344.1 million across four movies, though next weekend’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” will single-handedly change that calculus) and Paramount ($595 million across six movies including “Scary Movie” and “Scream 7”) — in this calendar year, according to Rentrak. That’s all thanks to Nolan. According to PostTrak, audiences cited the director as the main reason for buying a ticket to “The Odyssey.” Now that’s box office prowess.
	
		5. “The Odyssey” is holding better than Nolan’s other biggest movies	

	Nolan is behind “The Dark Knight” trilogy, widely considered the best comic book movies of all time. So it’s all the more remarkable that “The Odyssey” is pacing to become the director’s biggest film ever. Already, “The Odyssey” is exhibiting better staying power than those cinematic triumphs: “The Dark Knight” earned $75 million in its second weekend after opening to $158 million while “The Dark Knight Rises” collected $62 million in its second weekend after debuting to $160 million. In the decade-plus since those “Batman” movies, Nolan has become a brand unto himself. It’s safe to assume he’ll have carte blanche for his next big idea.
	
		6. “The Odyssey” hasn’t opened yet in China	

	Oh yeah, and “The Odyssey” has been steamrolling expectations without China, the world’s second-biggest moviegoing market. The country is rolling out the red-carpet treatment for “The Odyssey,” which is expected to play on nearly 800 Imax screens — and across thousands of standard auditoriums. Tickets haven’t gone on sale yet in mainland China, though the ticketing agency Maoyan Pro notes the “want to see” registrations for “The Odyssey” surpassed 252,000 by July 24, ahead of every other upcoming Hollywood release that’s been tracked by the platform. Nolan’s biggest movie in China is 2014’s sci-fi mind-bender “Interstellar” with $139 million, while his recent efforts were only modest successes in the country, with “Oppenheimer” earning $61 million, 2020’s time-bending “Tenet” generating $66 million, and 2017’s war drama “Dunkirk” making $50 million. China has been hostile to plenty of Hollywood blockbusters in recent years. Will “The Odyssey” have enough hype to beat the odds and become a hit in the Middle Kingdom?

schema.headline: ‘The Odyssey’ by the Numbers: 6 Ways Christopher Nolan’s Epic Is Shattering Box Office Expectations

title: Some Warner Bros. Execs Are Hoping States’ Antitrust Lawsuit Derails Paramount Deal
description: Privately, some top executives at Warner Bros. Discovery are rooting for the 12 states that have sued to block Paramount Skydance’s WBD takeover to
body:
Privately, some top executives at Warner Bros. Discovery are rooting for the 12 states that have sued to block Paramount Skydance’s WBD takeover to win in court and get the megadeal nixed.

	What’s obvious, according to multiple sources, is that there’s a sizable contingent at Warner Bros. of people who don’t want the merger with Paramount to happen. And the prevailing feeling among some at WBD clearly is a hope that the state attorneys general lawsuit will gum up the works long enough to cause the deal to fall apart. 
	

	In a memo distributed to WBD staff Monday afternoon, Simon Robinson, the company’s president of global experiences and studio operations and the executive who is leading the integration planning work, provided an update on the merger’s legal situation. “We are confident we will prevail and firmly believe this transaction is pro-competitive and will deliver significant benefits to the industry,” Robinson wrote.


	Paramount has agreed to put the Warner Bros. Discovery merger on ice pending the outcome of the trial in the antitrust case brought by 12 Democratic state AGs. That will delay the merger for at least a few months, and potentially up to a year or more, as the litigation plays out in court. The next step in the process will be negotiating for the trial date: Paramount wants it to start this fall, while the states want it to commence in 2027. The parties could potentially negotiate a settlement. But if the case goes to trial and the states prevail, Paramount would appeal the decision — and the merger could remain in legal limbo into the back half of 2027. 
	

	While some at Warner Bros. Discovery hold out hope that the Paramount pact will hit a legal landmine, others have accepted that the $111 billion merger will probably be consummated. Right now, says one WBD exec, “We need more information… People have more questions than anything else.” This person says, “I don’t pick up on resignation as much as people just wanting to know what they’re looking at. Like, are we planning for the upfront next year?” The answer to that, the exec adds, is that “you have to — because if this does drag out, it could take a year from now” before the deal closes.

	The new monthslong delay in the Paramount-WBD merger — and the looming prospect of mass layoffs if and when that happens — has left employees at both companies feeling unsure of what will happen and when. And uncertainty breeds anxiety.

	Paramount Skydance chief David Ellison penned a memo to the company’s employees Monday addressing the deal pause and acknowledging the less-than-ideal situation. “I know this additional uncertainty has been challenging, and I want to thank you for your continued patience, commitment and collective contributions,” he wrote. Ellison reiterated his confidence in Paramount’s legal case: “We believe this is the right path because the facts and the law are on our side, and a full hearing will demonstrate why the plaintiffs’ arguments should not prevail.”

	Ellison also included that familiar “it remains business as usual” refrain that managers trot out when big transactions are pending.

	For Warner Bros. Discovery, the merger agreement offers fairly wide latitude in how the company runs its business prior to the deal’s official close. Through the M&A process, for example, WBD has expanded HBO Max internationally. The company can enter into bundling agreements and acquire content, and has the flexibility to negotiate extensions or renewals with existing partners (such as the NHL or MLB) as well as content-licensing sales as long as the deals don’t extend past December 2028. But the longer the Paramount-WBD merger gets held up, the closer the Warner Bros. teams will be to bumping into that timeline.

	A source in WBD’s cable networks division says that, for now, it really is business as usual, “which is surprising.” All greenlit shows remain a go and the fall 2026 schedule is set, while new shows are being picked up already to air in 2027. The cable TV group is operating as if it really will be a year until Paramount-WBD could potentially close. There’s a fear right now that certain deals or decisions could be undone later under a combined company, this source adds, “but that was true of when WarnerMedia and Discovery merged, too.”
	

	Paramount definitely doesn’t want the merger delay to damage WBD’s long-term business outlook. “They need us to keep making money,” a Warner Bros. exec says.

	Across Warner Bros. Discovery, “people are in different head spaces” about the Paramount merger, says a company insider. For many leaders in the business units, “There’s the initial, ‘Oh wow, this is all happening,'” this person says. But with ongoing delays, “people get back to what they were doing.” The process of planning for the Paramount-WBD merger integration right now “is not a reality on a daily basis” for, say, someone working in the motion picture group.

	At Paramount, there’s also a mix of attitudes. “Some are like, ‘I can’t wait to bolt on XYZ’ to my business,'” says a source familiar with the company. “Others are thinking more like, ‘I don’t want to give up my fiefdom.'”

	Last week, a number of top execs at Warner Bros. Discovery came out for the Academy Museum premiere of HBO Max’s highly anticipated “Stuart Fails to Save the Universe,” a sci-fi spinoff of “The Big Bang Theory.” Those in attendance at the July 21 event included Warner Bros. TV’s Channing Dungey, Clancy Collins White and Brett Paul, and HBO Max’s Amy Gravitt. So more than a few gasps could be heard in the theater when “Stuart Fails to Save the Universe” co-creator Chuck Lorre dropped this bombshell in his opening remarks: “By the way, I don’t know if your phones have started buzzing yet, but big news: The Ellison-Paramount thing fell through.”

	Wait — what? Had everyone missed the biggest news of the summer as they got situated in their seats? Alas, it wasn’t meant to be: Lorre was doing a bit. “Chipotle is buying Warner Bros.,” he joked. “Chipotle WB.”

	The WBD execs in the room chuckled, but sighed. At the afterparty, the tension was real. As they attempted to stay cool as they mingled, attendees talked through scenarios about when and how the deal might still be stopped. Overall, the feeling that emerged from among those in the room was that the Paramount merger wasn’t fait accompli. At this point, it looks like there will be several more months of waiting before there’s clarity of the path forward.

	Jennifer Maas contributed to this article.

title: Massive Tribeca Fest Data Leak Exposes Jennifer Lawrence, Robert De Niro and More Celebs’ Contact Info; Meet the Man Who Discovered the Files
description: The Tribeca Festival suffered a data leak that exposed hundreds of thousands of records, as well as the contact information for thousands of celebri
body:
The Tribeca Festival suffered a data leak that exposed hundreds of thousands of records, as well as the contact information for thousands of celebrities, including Martin Scorsese, Francis Ford Coppola, Jennifer Lawrence, Angelina Jolie and festival co-founder Robert De Niro.

	Cybersecurity researcher Jeremiah Fowler revealed the leak in an ExpressVPN blog post over the weekend, claiming he’d uncovered a total of 666,369 exposed records with timestamps ranging from 2019 to 2026. Fowler, who works for Black Hills Information Security, publishes blogs on ExpressVPN and previously did cybersecurity for a software company in Kyiv, Ukraine, took time away from his European vacation to speak with Variety about discovering the data leak.
	

	“I’ve been a security researcher for about 15 years and I’m always looking for exposed data,” he says. “I’ve used a lot of different APIs and tools. This one I found using an IoT search engine, which is basically Google for websites but for connected devices like nanny cams, medical equipment or cloud storage databases.”


	Co-founded in 2002 by De Niro, Jane Rosenthal and Craig Hatkoff as a way to revitalize Lower Manhattan following the September 11 attacks, the fest takes place annually in New York City, and has played host to the premieres of everything from “The Avengers” to “The Handmaid’s Tale,” while awarding films like “Let the Right One In.” Tribeca Festival’s 2026 edition, marking its 25th anniversary, ran from June 3-14.

	The festival issued a statement, with a spokesperson asserting, “None of the talent referenced in recent reporting had personal contact information disclosed. The vast majority of the information consisted of public-facing business contact information, including PR representatives, talent representatives, front office email addresses, information from the Festival website, and other information that was already publicly available. All information was removed promptly upon discovery.”While the majority of the Tribeca Festival data was not sensitive, consisting of things like marketing materials, press kits and promotional images, there was a backup .dump file that “contained potentially sensitive information,” including a folder named “contacts” that had 13,535 entries, including “the names, addresses, phone numbers and emails” of prominent filmmakers like Scorsese, Coppola, Guillermo del Toro, Ron Howard, and others, as well as popular actors such as De Niro, Lawrence, Jolie, Morgan Freeman, Rami Malek, Eva Mendes and Michael J. Fox. Fowler noted, however, that some of the contact fields were missing data or contained the contacts of assistants, managers or publicists in lieu of a personal email or phone number. (Variety is still awaiting comment from the Tribeca Festival, which disputed some of Fowler’s findings by phone.)
	



	

					A screenshot of a portion of the data leak with sensitive information redacted.
									Jermaine Fowler
	



	“Normally, when you back up something, you don’t keep it in a production environment,” he says of Tribeca’s folly. “You either take it offline or put it in a separate database, that way it’s your fail-safe in case something does go wrong. One document had around 135,000 contacts, and I’m assuming these would be people who signed up for mailing lists and people that go to events. The celebrities were in something called ‘contacts,’ and that had around 13,000.”

	He adds, “[Tribeca] kind of disputed that some — not all — of the contacts may have been managers or assistants, but I saw a lot of consumer email accounts, like Google or Yahoo.”

	According to Fowler, the Tribeca Festival committed “a human error of leaving the backup file in the database, and the backup file was in plain text, unencrypted.” If it was encrypted, he wouldn’t have been able to access it. But every one of the data points, he explains, was available to anyone with an internet connection, so anyone could create an account with a IoT search engine and view the data in a browser like Chrome, Firefox or Safari.

	While the Tribeca Festival made a mistake in leaving the data exposed, Fowler commended the actions the fest took in the wake of his revelations, admitting the fest “responded very fast and professionally.” Plus, he “didn’t see any evidence of anyone else accessing it,” since normally data that’s been exposed for a lengthy period of time would come with automatic ransomware posts requesting various amounts of bitcoin, and those weren’t there.

	He warns that exposing people’s personal data, such as email accounts, poses an even bigger threat in the era of AI, which has democratized hacking.
	

	“The creativity level of criminals has shot up beyond anything. AI gives anyone the ability to do things that non-technical people couldn’t do before,” he reasons. “Now, you can feed it information and ask it to create a phishing email. You could use Claude, ask it to create malware, insert it in a document saying, ‘Check out this script!’ and send it to 135,000 people, and somebody’s going to open it. It’s a very, very big issue.”

	As a seasoned cybersecurity researcher, Fowler maintains that his mission isn’t to embarrass companies, but rather show them where their vulnerabilities lie and get them to improve their cybersecurity so that their information doesn’t fall into the wrong hands in the future.

	“The purpose of my report and findings are not to throw organizations under the bus,” he says. “Organizations that do have a data incident statistically don’t have another one for three to five years since it becomes a primary focus and you dedicate the resources to penetration testing and vulnerability scans. It happens often, especially in industries unrelated to technology.”

title: Savannah Guthrie Posts New Video Urging Mother’s Kidnappers to ‘Do the Right Thing’: ‘Tell Us Where to Look for Her’
description:
For the first time since April, Savannah Guthrie posted a new video to Instagram directly addressing her mother’s kidnappers.

	“I’m coming on today
body:
For the first time since April, Savannah Guthrie posted a new video to Instagram directly addressing her mother’s kidnappers.

	“I’m coming on today with a very specific message. It has been months since our mom was taken from us. Our family is in agony. We are in a nightmare that will not end. Nothing about our situation has changed,” the “Today” host said. Her mom, Nancy, went missing in February and has yet to be found. “We have done our part, and we will never stop looking for her. We will always ache for her and feel that hole in our hearts.”
	

	Guthrie then tried to appeal directly to the people who took her mother or may know where she is now. “The world can be a cruel and unforgiving place, and I know that you have tried to do things the right way. So I’m asking you, begging you to do the right thing now,” she continued. “Make the right choice. Help us find her. Tell us where to look for her. I truly believe it is never too late to do the right thing. Help us bring this situation to an end. For all of us, no matter where we’ve been and what we’ve done, I believe there is always a way home. Please make the right choice.”


	Nancy went missing on Feb. 1 after she did not show up to her usual Sunday church service. The next day, the Pima County Sheriff’s Department called her disappearance a presumed kidnapping after they found concerning evidence at her home in Tucson, Ariz.  The FBI joined in the search for Nancy and posted a $100,000 reward for information leading to her recovery. It was later increased to $200,000 and then $1 million on Feb. 24.

	On Feb. 10, the FBI recovered footage from a destroyed Ring doorbell camera at Nancy’s home that showed the only person of interest in the case. The video shows “a male, approximately 5’9” – 5’10” tall, with an average build” approaching Nancy’s front door while armed and wearing a hiking backpack. After the footage was released, the FBI said it had received more than 13,000 tips about Nancy, but no arrests have been made.
	

	Guthrie has posted several videos on her social media asking for her mother’s kidnappers to return her safely.

	“We also know that she may be lost,” she said on Feb. 24. “She may already be gone. She may have already gone home to the lord that she loves and is dancing in heaven with her mom and her dad and with her beloved brother Pierce and with our daddy. If this is what is to be, then we will accept it. But we need to know where she is. We need her to come home.”

            Blake Garrett -- best known for his role in "How to Eat Fried Worms" -- was found unresponsive next to his bed in a sober living house ... with rolled dollar bills, a lighter, and foil with burnt residue nearby.
      
    
            TMZ obtained the former child actor's full autopsy report, which describes the scene at the Tulsa residence where he was found dead back in February.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The Oklahoma Medical Examiner previously determined Garrett died from acute fentanyl toxicity and ruled the manner of death an accident ... and the autopsy shows alcohol testing came back negative.
      

            The autopsy also found diffuse swelling in Garrett's brain ... and noted he had shingles without complications, with lesions in various stages of healing.
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... Garrett's mother, Carol, told us her son had recently been diagnosed with shingles -- and she believed he may have accidentally overdosed while trying to manage the pain after three years of sobriety.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            It looks like her worst fears were realized.
      
    
            Garrett played Plug in the 2006 comedy "How to Eat Fried Worms" ... earning a Young Artist Award alongside the movie's young ensemble cast.
      
    
            He was only 33.

D4vd Murder Trial
                          Defense Claims Celeste's Family Was Cool With Them Hanging Out

                              July 27, 2026
                            11:38 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Celeste Rivas' family knew she was hanging out with D4vd before she was found dead in his car ... and in some cases, signed off on her traveling with him on tour and overseas, despite initially saying they didn't know him ... at least according to his defense team.
      
    
            D4vd's attorneys presented evidence Monday -- during the fifth day of his preliminary hearing -- suggesting the family knew something was going on between Celeste and D4vd and did nothing to stop it.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            Celeste's sister allegedly traveled with them to one of D4vd's shows in Las Vegas ... and a notarized travel form to her parents showed they allegedly gave consent for Celeste to travel to London for a week in 2024 without any other family members.
      

            These allegations could be seen as flying in the face of what Celeste's father, Jesus Rivas, told TMZ in May, through his attorney Patrick Steinfeld ... when he claimed he never "had any contact with this guy."
      
    
            At the time, Jesus also said the family never received any money from D4vd or anyone in his family.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As TMZ reported ... there was a slew of evidence presented by prosecutors during the preliminary hearing, which included grisly photos of the Celeste's decomposed body ... along with several alleged text messages which prosecutors argued showed the two had a sexual relationship when she was 14 years old.
      
    
            D4vd is charged with Celeste's murder ... with prosecutors alleging the singer killed her because she threatened to expose their illegal sexual relationship. He has pleaded not guilty.
